About the Role: 

An exciting opportunity is presented to work within the Northern Adelaide Local Health Network as a Business Consultant within Mental Health Services (Forensic and Mental Health). 

The Business Consultant provides expert and timely resource management information, advice and support to ensure that business objectives of the Divisions are met.

The Business Consultant contributes as an equal and integral team member towards service planning and decision making in support of the Divisional Directors, who are responsible for coordinating the business of the Division.

The Business Consultant significantly contributes to the effective and efficient functioning of the service, by providing expert and timely resource management information, advice and support to ensure that business objectives of the Divisions are met.

To be eligible for this position, you must have an appropriate degree in accounting, finance or economics majoring in accounting

About You: 

In this role you will have strong interpersonal and communication skills which will enable you to successfully problem solve, resolve conflicts and negotiate, including the ability to engage in difficult conversations, whilst building and maintaining relationships. An ability to effectively manage multiple, diverse and competing priorities and demonstrated resilience within a stressful and complex environment is essential to this role. 

You will be joining a dynamic and expanding Local Health Network that is committed to delivering contemporary, innovative and high-quality health services within modern facilities. 

This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to a passionate, highly driven, dedicated and progressive team. 

About Adelaide: 

Adelaide is consistently recognised as a city that artfully combines its compact charm and world-class cuisine with picturesque nature escapes. Ranked one of the worlds "Most Liveable Cities" and "Most Beautiful Cities", Adelaide provides something for everyone combining a wonderful mix of nature with nearby beaches, rolling hills and wildlife and culinary delights with fine dining restaurants, award-winning cafes, bustling food markets and booming boutique bars. Events like the LIV Golf, SANTOS Tour Down Under, Adelaide Fringe and the Adelaide Cabaret Festival add extra appeal to living here. 

About Us: 

The Northern Adelaide Local Health Network (NALHN) is a leading provider of public healthcare services in South Australia, and one of the largest employers in northern Adelaide. 

NALHN serves over 400,000 people in northern Adelaide with a comprehensive range of high-quality healthcare services, including emergency, surgical, obstetric, neonatal, paediatric, oncology, geriatric, palliative care and rehabilitation, and mental health care, as well as primary health care services with a focus on community health promotion and chronic disease management. 

With a commitment for ongoing upgrades to our facilities and the introduction of new services, our priority is delivering exceptional health and wellbeing services that enhance the quality of life for our community. 

With over 7,000 employees, NALHN emphasises quality care and a supportive work environment guided by respect, integrity, and accountability. Our core values foster excellence, innovation, and equitable health outcomes. 

At NALHN Everyone Has a Story, Everyone Matters, Everyone Contributes and Everyone Grows. 

Our Local Health Network Sites and Services: 

NALHN provides a range of hospital (inpatient), outpatient, community and home-based services across multiple sites in Adelaide's north and north-eastern suburbs, including Aboriginal health, mental health, and GP services. 

Lyell McEwin Hospital - the major hospital in northern Adelaide for emergency care, complex and multi-day surgery, medicine, obstetric, paediatrics and outpatient services. 

Modbury Hospital - a general hospital with emergency care, elective surgery, medicine, outpatient and sub-acute services, rehabilitation, geriatric and palliative care. 

Mental Health Services - adult and older persons mental health services and statewide forensic mental health services, across hospital and community settings. 

Watto Purrunna Aboriginal Primary Health Care Services - provides culturally responsive primary healthcare services for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in-hospital and across four community sites. 

Primary Health Care Services - including GP Plus sites at Elizabeth, Modbury and Gilles Plains.

Position: Retail Manager (General)
Type: Full-time
Employer: Goyal Companies Pty Ltd
Location: Cairns City QLD 4870
Salary: $80,000 p/a
About the Business:
Goyal Companies Pty Ltd operates a busy Subway franchise located in the heart of Cairns, Queensland. As part of the globally recognised Subway brand, the store delivers fresh, made-to-order submarine sandwiches, salads, and wraps to a diverse customer base of locals, shoppers, and tourists. The business is committed to excellence in food quality, customer service, and operational standards while fostering a supportive, team-oriented workplace culture that values accountability, continuous improvement, and work-life balance for its leadership team.
About the Position:
This full-time Retail Manager (General) role has been created to professionalise the day-to-day operations of the Subway store, reducing the current heavy reliance on the business owner. Reporting directly to the owner/franchisee, the Retail Manager will take full responsibility for leading operations, staff management, compliance, inventory, and customer service excellence. This key leadership position will enable the business to operate independently and sustainably, supporting long-term growth and allowing the owner to focus on strategic development.
Key Responsibilities:
Organise, direct and control the daily operations of the restaurant to ensure efficient and profitable performance in line with Subway franchise standards.
Manage inventory levels, purchasing, stock control, and wastage to maintain optimal product availability and quality.
Lead staff recruitment, training, rostering, supervision, and performance management to build a capable and motivated team.
Uphold exceptional customer service standards, resolve complaints promptly, and monitor feedback to drive continuous improvement.
Ensure full compliance with food safety, workplace health and safety, franchise policies, and all regulatory requirements.
Monitor sales, labour costs, and operational expenses, implementing strategies to improve profitability and efficiency.
Oversee marketing activities, promotional campaigns, and third-party delivery platforms to support business growth.
Manage operational issues, staff shortages, and day-to-day decision-making to ensure business continuity without constant owner involvement.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Minimum Diploma in Business Management, Retail Management or Hospitality Management (particularly for fast food or quick service restaurants).
Minimum 1 year in retail food management, with strong leadership and people management skills.
Demonstrated experience managing retail, fast-food, hospitality or franchise operations, including inventory control, workforce management, food safety, WHS, and compliance.
Proven ability to analyse business performance, implement operational improvements, and deliver excellent customer service.
Strong communication, organisational, problem-solving and leadership skills with the ability to foster a positive team culture.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

•	Apply a deep understanding of the consumer in response to all briefs
•	Translate consumer understanding into actionable, fact-based strategies

•	Create the vision and strategy and then inspire others to work towards it
•	Deliver excellence in execution

Salary - $80k-$100k package

Our client, Khosa Concrete & Landscaping Pty Ltd, located in Huntingdale, Western Australia, is a growing construction business specialising in high-quality concreting, landscaping and outdoor construction solutions throughout the Perth metropolitan area. The company delivers a broad range of residential and commercial projects, including concrete driveways, pathways, patios, retaining walls, paving, fencing, timber structures, artificial turf installations and complete landscape transformations. 

Due to continued business growth and an increasing volume of construction projects, our client is seeking an experienced and motivated Carpenter to join its skilled construction team. The successful applicant will undertake a variety of carpentry works associated with building interiors, outdoor living spaces and structural construction, while ensuring projects are completed safely, efficiently and to the highest quality standards.

Key Responsibilities:

-	Read and interpret construction drawings, plans and specifications to determine materials, dimensions and installation requirements. 
-	Measure, cut, shape, assemble and install timber, plywood and other building materials to required specifications. 
-	Construct, install and repair timber frameworks, wall frames, floor systems, roof structures, partitions and ceilings. 
-	Install doors, windows, skirting boards, architraves, staircases, cabinetry and other interior and exterior timber fittings. 
-	Build and install pergolas, decking, fencing, gates and other outdoor timber structures. 
-	Carry out first-fix and second-fix carpentry works for residential and commercial building projects. 
-	Undertake formwork construction where required to support building and landscaping projects. 
-	Repair and maintain existing timber structures, fixtures and fittings to ensure structural integrity and appearance. 
-	Operate, maintain and inspect carpentry tools, machinery and equipment in a safe and efficient manner. 
-	Estimate material requirements and assist in ordering timber and construction materials. 
-	Ensure all carpentry works comply with Australian building codes, project specifications and workplace health and safety requirements. 
-	Liaise professionally with clients, supervisors and other trades to ensure projects are completed on time and to a high standard.

Skills & Qualifications

-	AQF Certificate III in Carpentry (or equivalent trade qualification), including at least two years of structured on-the-job training, or AQF Certificate IV in a relevant trade.
-	Minimum one year of relevant full-time experience as a Carpenter.
-	Ability to accurately read and interpret construction drawings, plans and specifications.
-	Strong knowledge of construction methods, building materials and safe work practices.
-	High attention to detail with excellent workmanship and problem-solving abilities.
-	Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team environment.
-	Good organisational and time management skills with the ability to meet project deadlines.
-	Sound understanding of Australian Workplace Health and Safety requirements.

Please note only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and your application will be treated as strictly confidential.

Partnering closely with leaders across the organisation, you will help drive key people initiatives, support operational excellence and contribute to the development of scalable people practices and frameworks. This is a business that's very much in a phase of "creating the plane while flying it." As such, we're looking for someone who thrives in evolving environments, can comfortably navigate ambiguity, and enjoys bringing structure, process and practical solutions while maintaining momentum. Northern Adelaide Local Health Network - Finance Division - Elizabeth Vale

Salary: $105,747 - $111,854 p.a. (pro rata) plus Superannuation and Salary Sacrifice benefits - ASO6

Ongoing-Full-Time (Multiple Positions) 

About the Role: 

An exciting opportunity is presented to work within the Northern Adelaide Local Health Network as a Business Consultant. 

The Business Consultant provides expert and timely resource management information, advice and support to ensure that business objectives of the Divisions are met.

The Business Consultant contributes as an equal and integral team member towards service planning and decision making in support of the Divisional Directors, who are responsible for coordinating the business of the Division.

The Business Consultant significantly contributes to the effective and efficient functioning of the service, by providing expert and timely resource management information, advice and support to ensure that business objectives of the Divisions are met.

To be eligible for this position, you must have an appropriate degree in accounting, finance or economics majoring in accounting

About You: 

In this role you will have strong interpersonal and communication skills which will enable you to successfully problem solve, resolve conflicts and negotiate, including the ability to engage in difficult conversations, whilst building and maintaining relationships. An ability to effectively manage multiple, diverse and competing priorities and demonstrated resilience within a stressful and complex environment is essential to this role. 

You will be joining a dynamic and expanding Local Health Network that is committed to delivering contemporary, innovative and high-quality health services within modern facilities. 

This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to a passionate, highly driven, dedicated and progressive team. 

About Adelaide: 

Adelaide is consistently recognised as a city that artfully combines its compact charm and world-class cuisine with picturesque nature escapes. Ranked one of the worlds "Most Liveable Cities" and "Most Beautiful Cities", Adelaide provides something for everyone combining a wonderful mix of nature with nearby beaches, rolling hills and wildlife and culinary delights with fine dining restaurants, award-winning cafes, bustling food markets and booming boutique bars. Events like the LIV Golf, SANTOS Tour Down Under, Adelaide Fringe and the Adelaide Cabaret Festival add extra appeal to living here. 

About Us: 

The Northern Adelaide Local Health Network (NALHN) is a leading provider of public healthcare services in South Australia, and one of the largest employers in northern Adelaide. 

NALHN serves over 400,000 people in northern Adelaide with a comprehensive range of high-quality healthcare services, including emergency, surgical, obstetric, neonatal, paediatric, oncology, geriatric, palliative care and rehabilitation, and mental health care, as well as primary health care services with a focus on community health promotion and chronic disease management. 

With a commitment for ongoing upgrades to our facilities and the introduction of new services, our priority is delivering exceptional health and wellbeing services that enhance the quality of life for our community. 

With over 7,000 employees, NALHN emphasises quality care and a supportive work environment guided by respect, integrity, and accountability. Our core values foster excellence, innovation, and equitable health outcomes. 

At NALHN Everyone Has a Story, Everyone Matters, Everyone Contributes and Everyone Grows. 

Our Local Health Network Sites and Services: 

NALHN provides a range of hospital (inpatient), outpatient, community and home-based services across multiple sites in Adelaide's north and north-eastern suburbs, including Aboriginal health, mental health, and GP services. 

Lyell McEwin Hospital - the major hospital in northern Adelaide for emergency care, complex and multi-day surgery, medicine, obstetric, paediatrics and outpatient services. 

Modbury Hospital - a general hospital with emergency care, elective surgery, medicine, outpatient and sub-acute services, rehabilitation, geriatric and palliative care. 

Mental Health Services - adult and older persons mental health services and statewide forensic mental health services, across hospital and community settings. 

Watto Purrunna Aboriginal Primary Health Care Services - provides culturally responsive primary healthcare services for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in-hospital and across four community sites. 

Primary Health Care Services - including GP Plus sites at Elizabeth, Modbury and Gilles Plains. 
 
Benefits of working at NALHN: 
 
From salary packaging to flexible working arrangements, a large range of opportunities for movement and career progression, you'll find there are lots of benefits of working with Northern Adelaide Local Health Network. 
 
Salary packaging is an option for saving money by paying for some of your everyday expenses from your salary before it is taxed. 
 
Relocation assistance may be available for successful applicants from interstate or overseas. 
 
NALHN supports and fosters a culture in which employees feel they belong and feel safe at work. The culture aims to encourage all people to use their talents and to be valued and rewarded for their contributions. 
 
SA Health is committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence. 
 
We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if you have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best. 
 
The South Australian public sector promotes diversity and flexible ways of working including part-time. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the flexible working arrangements for this role. 
 
Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check.

Accreditation is provided by the Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission. See our National Police Certificate accredited bodies page for links to lodge screening requests.
